name: Apache Paimon
tagline: Streaming lakehouse table format with LSM-based upserts and changelogs, born in Apache Flink.
description: Apache Paimon (formerly Flink Table Store) is a lake table format designed for real-time updates: each bucket is an LSM tree of Parquet or ORC files, so primary-key tables absorb high-rate upserts and deletes from Flink CDC while producing a changelog that downstream streaming jobs can consume. It offers snapshots, time travel, tags and branches, and is readable by Flink, Spark, Trino, StarRocks, Doris and Python. Paimon fits streaming lakehouse pipelines, especially CDC into the lake; Iceberg has broader engine support for mostly-append batch data.

pricing.notes: Free; used in Alibaba Cloud Realtime Compute for Apache Flink and other managed Flink services.

scale.notes: Scales with the compute engine and object storage; bucketed tables parallelize writes.

queryLanguages: SQL (via Flink, Spark, Trino, StarRocks, Doris)
strengths: LSM-based primary-key tables handle high-rate upserts from CDC
Native changelog output enables incremental streaming pipelines
Snapshots, tags, branches and time travel
Readable by Flink, Spark, Trino, StarRocks and Doris
Can expose tables in Iceberg-compatible metadata
weaknesses: A table format, not a query engine: needs Flink/Spark/Trino on top
Compaction tuning matters for read performance
Smaller engine ecosystem than Iceberg or Delta
useCases: Streaming CDC from databases into the lake
